current_activity: Taken under command of the 6th Airborne Division and deployed on the extreme left of the front, on the coast
notes: Event date: 13 August 1944 (Stacey, p. 265; Ellis, vol. I, p. 448). Event definition: Newly arrived from England, the brigade is taken under command of the 6th Airborne Division, holding the left of I Corps east of the Orne, and is deployed on the extreme left on the coast. Event support: two source families (Stacey, the Canadian official history and Ellis, the British official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 265: "On 13 August the Netherlands and Belgian contingents"; "both newly arrived from England, were taken under command of the 6th Airborne Division and deployed on the extreme left on the coast"; Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 448: "Belgian and Dutch contingents newly arrived from England". Location: Merville-Franceville-Plage, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is a representative point on the coast at the left of the 6th Airborne Division line; precision 10 km. Location support: the place is a representative point (inferred value): Stacey gives only "the extreme left on the coast"; Merville-Franceville is the coastal end of the airborne line east of the Orne and the first place the brigade liberated (17 August, Wikipedia). Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

current_activity: Advance along the Channel coast with the 6th Airborne Division: liberates Merville-Franceville in the evening
notes: Event date: 17 August 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: With the British and Dutch troops of the 6th Airborne Division the brigade begins clearing the Channel coast east of the Orne (Operation Paddle) and liberates Merville-Franceville-Plage in the evening. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Normandy invasion: "Clearing the Channel coast from 17 August with British and Dutch (Prinses Irene Brigade) troops of the 6th Airborne Division. Merville-Franceville-Plage was liberated in the evening". Location: Merville-Franceville-Plage, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names the place liberated on 17 August. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

current_activity: Advance along the coast: takes Villers-sur-Mer and Deauville
notes: Event date: 22 August 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: After Dives-sur-Mer, Cabourg and Houlgate (21 August) the brigade takes Villers-sur-Mer and Deauville. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Normandy invasion: "The brigade took Villers-sur-Mer and Deauville on 22 August". Location: Deauville, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Deauville. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

current_activity: Advance along the coast: takes Trouville-sur-Mer and Honfleur at the mouth of the Seine
notes: Event date: 24 August 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: The brigade takes Trouville-sur-Mer and Honfleur, at the mouth of the Seine. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Normandy invasion: "Trouville-sur-Mer and Honfleur at the mouth of the Seine on 24 August". Location: Honfleur, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Honfleur. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

current_activity: Reunited with its armoured vehicles at Foulbec on the Seine estuary; placed under the 49th Division on 28 August
notes: Event date: 26 August 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: The armoured vehicles, detached to British units during the coastal advance, rejoin the rest of the brigade at Foulbec; on 28 August the brigade is placed under the 49th Infantry Division to mop up the Seine estuary and help in the siege of Le Havre. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Normandy invasion: "The Belgian armoured vehicles were reunited with the rest of the brigade on 26 August at Foulbec"; "On 28 August 1944, the brigade was placed under the British 49th Infantry Division". Location: Foulbec, Eure (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Foulbec. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

source_locator: R144: section Belgium and the Netherlands
current_activity: Transferred to the Second Army: reaches the Belgian border on 3 September and Brussels on 4 September
notes: Event date: 4 September 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: Transferred to the Second Army on 2 September and ordered to the Belgian border as quickly as possible, the brigade reaches the French-Belgian border on 3 September after an overnight journey and enters Brussels the next day, just after the British. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Belgium and the Netherlands: "On 2 September, the brigade and the Dutch Princess Irene Brigade had been transferred to the Second Army"; "after an overnight journey and continued to Brussels the following day, just after the British". Location: Brussels with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the city; the brigade is not placed more exactly, so precision 10 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Brussels. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

source_locator: R144: section Belgium and the Netherlands
current_activity: Albert Canal bridgehead: helps to capture Leopoldsburg (Bourg-Leopold), freeing 900 political prisoners
notes: Event date: 11 September 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: The brigade fights in the battle for the Albert Canal bridgehead and helps to capture Leopoldsburg, liberating 900 political prisoners. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Belgium and the Netherlands: "On 11 September 1944, the brigade participated in a battle at the Albert Canal bridgehead and helped to capture Leopoldsburg". Location: Leopoldsburg, Limburg (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Leopoldsburg. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

source_locator: R144: section Belgium and the Netherlands
current_activity: Reaches the Wessem canal and liberates Thorn, in Dutch Limburg
notes: Event date: 25 September 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: Having reached the Dutch border on 22 September, the brigade reaches the Wessem canal and liberates the town of Thorn. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Belgium and the Netherlands: "On 25 September 1944 the brigade reached the Wessem canal"; "In the small Dutch border town of Thorn, a bridge has been named in honour of its liberation on 25 September 1944". Location: Thorn, Limburg (Netherlands) (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Thorn as liberated by the brigade on 25 September. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

source_locator: R144: section Belgium and the Netherlands
current_activity: Relieved from the front on the Wessem canal and moved into reserve at Leuven to reorganise
notes: Event date: 17 November 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: After fighting on the Wessem canal, at its height on 11 November, the brigade is relieved from the front and moves into reserve at Leuven, where it is reorganised as a full brigade. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Piron Brigade (Independent Belgian Brigade), section Belgium and the Netherlands: "Its campaign in the Netherlands lasted until 17 November, when it was relieved from the front and moved into reserve in Leuven". Location: Leuven, Flemish Brabant (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Leuven. Location caveat: Wikipedia says the brigade was withdrawn six days after 11 November and moved into reserve on 17 November; the row is placed at Leuven on 17 November. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).

current_activity: On the "island" under the 1st Canadian Armoured Brigade: Belgian infantry with Calgary tanks seize Opheusden
notes: Event date: 18 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 581; under Brigadier Murphy from 12 April, p. 570). Event definition: Holding the "island" between the Neder Rijn and the Waal under Brigadier Murphy's 1st Canadian Armoured Brigade, Belgian infantry supported by "B" Squadron of The Calgary Regiment seize Opheusden as Murphy's front conforms to the British advance; the enemy retires behind the canal at Ochten. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 581: "Belgian infantry, supported by"; "Squadron of The Calgary Regiment, seized Opheusden on the 18th"; p. 570: "Murphy was given the 1st Belgian Infantry Brigade (two battalions)". Location: Opheusden, Gelderland (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey p. 581 names Opheusden. Commander: Colonel B. E. M. Piron (Jean-Baptiste Piron) commands the brigade (Stacey, p. 265, note; Wikipedia).
